original_question: Can the McKay correspondence be generalized at the level of derived categories to the wild case?
target_in_paper: Section 12, Problem 12.1, together with its immediately following explanatory paragraph: the paper asks for a wild analogue of the derived McKay correspondence, and then explains that if a crepant resolution exists, the classical comparison would be between D^b(Coh Y) and the bounded derived category of G-equivariant coherent sheaves on the representation space, but that this naive form cannot survive in the wild case. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2107.07073))
correct_elements: Your draft is already on the right target: it correctly identifies that the paper is asking about a derived-categorical version of the McKay correspondence in the wild setting, not about the stringy-motive formulation from earlier sections. It is also close in wording to the paper’s own Problem 12.1. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2107.07073))
missing_details: The paper is working in the quotient-singularity setup over an algebraically closed base field; “wild” means the characteristic is p>0 and p divides the order of the finite group. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2107.07073))

For actions on affine space, the standing assumptions are that the finite-group action is linear and, unless otherwise noted, has no pseudo-reflections; Section 2.3 also states the action is faithful. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2107.07073))

The precise geometric objects should be named: if V is the affine space with G-action and X=V/G is the quotient, the question is posed under the additional hypothesis that X admits a crepant resolution Y→X. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2107.07073))

The classical comparison that motivates the problem is specifically between the bounded derived category of coherent sheaves on Y and the bounded derived category of G-equivariant coherent sheaves on V. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2107.07073))

A paper-faithful standalone version must include the key caveat that this classical equivalence cannot literally hold in the wild case, because the equivariant coherent-sheaf category has infinite global dimension there. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2107.07073))

So the real research question is not merely whether some derived generalization exists, but what should replace the usual equivariant derived category on the wild side; the paper explicitly suggests that such a replacement may require higher structures from noncommutative algebraic geometry. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2107.07073))
refined_question: Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic p>0, let G be a finite group with p dividing |G| acting linearly, faithfully, and without pseudo-reflections on an affine space V= A_k^d, and set X=V/G. Assume that X admits a crepant resolution f:Y→X. What object on the “representation-theoretic” side should replace the bounded derived category of G-equivariant coherent sheaves on V so as to yield a wild derived McKay correspondence with D^b(Coh Y), given that the classical equivalence D^b(Coh Y) ≅ D^b(Coh^G V) cannot hold in the wild case because Coh^G(V) has infinite global dimension? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2107.07073))
justification: The draft is essentially a paraphrase of Section 12, Problem 12.1, so that is the exact target in the paper. The nearby context supplies the hidden assumptions needed to make it standalone: the paper’s global convention on the base field and linear/no-pseudo-reflection setup, the standard quotient V/G framework from Section 2.3, and the extra hypothesis in Section 12 that a crepant resolution exists. Most importantly, the paragraph after Problem 12.1 shows that the paper is not asking for the literal wild validity of the usual equivalence with D^b(Coh^G V); it says this never holds in the wild case and therefore asks for an alternative, possibly higher-categorical replacement. The refined question keeps exactly that scope and does not broaden the problem beyond the paper’s intent. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2107.07073))
